text: still dont believe it. is the array doing ranges of colors or is it listing every single pixel
resolution: User did not believe the run count and asked whether the array does ranges or lists every pixel. Proved BOTH with raw data: (1) the encoder ranges — flat row 512 encodes 1024 pixels as just [[193,0],[433,593],[398,null]] (3 entries) and busy rows use [4,1]/[5,0] runs where adjacent pixels match; (2) the raw stored bytes genuinely alternate per-pixel — row 50 cols 500-539 interleave d97757/e7ae8d one pixel at a time. So 100k runs is real data, not a codec flaw. The discovery: the texture is the user's 3 colours STIPPLED at the pixel level in transition zones (brush edge_coverage feather in paintable.zig) rather than flat — which is both why it won't RLE and arguably a crispness regression. Hardening the brush to flat storage is the lever where the user's RLE instinct pays off. Awaiting decision.
